newsitem.title: INDIA: Cyclone near India's Gujarat begins to weaken.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone near India's Gujarat begins to weaken.

text.p: Indian weather forecasters said on Friday a cyclone currently moving across the Arabian Sea and expected to strike India's western state of Gujarat later in the afternoon had weakened as it moved closer to the coast.
"The morning's severe cyclonic storm has weakened into a cyclonic storm," the India Meteorological Department said in a noon forecast.

The cyclone, expected to bring rains and strong winds of 50 kmph to 60 kmph to nearby Bombay, was originally forecast to hit the coast Thursday night but then slowed as it passed over the Arabian Sea, the weather officials said.
The cyclone is now about 100 km off India's western coast.
"It is likely to move in a northerly direction and cross the Gujarat coast between Bhavnagar and Porbandar close to Veraval by afternoon today," the statement said.
The three towns are minor ports located on the south Gujarat coast, about 330 km northwest of Bombay.
Bombay is located in neighbouring Maharashtra state.
Weather bureau officials in Bombay said the city can expect the bad weather to continue until late Friday.
Fishermen have been warned to stay in port during the next 24 hours, they said. -- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
